SMTO-HTTP-0037 — The service didn't accept SMTO's sign-in

GUID: ad246145-1b52-4afc-9a95-5f51c8fa3b3c
Slug: http-credentials-rejected
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service turned down the sign-in or its access check. That can mean wrong details, missing permission, or a reply SMTO couldn't understand; the reply doesn't say which.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and re-enter the values under Authentication, such as Password, API key, Token or Client secret. Watch for extra spaces. An expired or mistyped value is the most common reason a sign-in is turned down.
  2. Ask the owner of the service account to confirm it is active and allowed to do what the task asked. The service may recognise the account but still not let it use this part of the service.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. When it shows Authenticated, run the task again. Testing first confirms the sign-in works before the task tries again.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated and the task's request is accepted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the service account. Never paste passwords, keys or tokens into a task, chat message, screenshot or the details you share.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Authentication was rejected (401/403 from the login or resource endpoint), the OAuth token endpoint returned an unmapped error, or the OAuth reply was not an object; the failing credential field is not identified.

What this means

  • The login endpoint returned 401/403, OAuth returned an unmapped error, or OAuth acceptance received a non-object document; this classification does not identify a bad credential field. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The login endpoint returned 401/403, OAuth returned an unmapped error, or OAuth acceptance received a non-object document; this classification does not identify a bad credential field.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe HTTP/OAuth status and document shape; distinguish access policy, invalid client/grant and malformed provider responses.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the recorded authentication status and response and the account's permissions or access policy, then correct only the credential, OAuth client setting or response mapping the response implicates. A 403 usually indicates missing authorization rather than a wrong password.
  • Check the actual authentication response, permission and access policy; correct only the established credential, configuration or response-format problem.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The documented authentication flow returns a valid accepted session for the intended account.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-HTTP-0081 — The service refused access for this account
  • SMTO-HTTP-0038 — SMTO couldn't find the service's sign-in address
  • SMTO-HTTP-0044 — SMTO couldn't confirm the service's security certificate
